newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses climb with Dow but remain uneasy.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses climb with Dow but remain uneasy.

text.p: European stocks got off to a robust start on Thursday on the heels of the third consecutive overnight surge by U.S. blue chips only to settle back slightly by mid-morning.
On the currency markets the dollar edged lower against the yen, pressured by Japan's widening trade surplus with the United States and political pressure for higher Japanese interest rates.

European equities were encouraged by the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which jumped 93 points or 1.4 percent on Wednesday. Wall Street was ignited by a sharp rally in tobacco stocks on hopes that the industry was nearing a settlement on U.S. litigation.
But not all the news from the United States was encouraging as healthy economic data revived concerns the economy may be expanding too rapidly.
"People are getting twitchy about the Dow," said one London-based trader.

Frankfurt blue chips posted the morning's strongest gains, with the DAX index rising nearly one percent. Daimler Benz fell sharply after disappointment at an analyst meeting following the company results announcement on Wednesday.

London shares proved more reserved, ticking just a few points higher. After adding 28 pence on Wednesday tobacco company B.A.T led the early movers, rising five pence although it then shed its gains to trade flat for the session.

Britain reported slightly lower-than-expected March inflation, which rose 0.3 percent in the month versus market expectations of 0.4 percent although the dip in inflationary pressure failed to help the market.

Fears over near-term U.S. and UK interest rate rises, the continuing pressure of a strong currency and worries over post-election changes to corporate taxes are all weighing on sentiment, traders said.
"We are now two weeks away from an election and the volatility is concerning people," one said. "People do not want this market to run away with itself. That is why we haven't reflected Wall Street."
French blue chips also gained nearly half a percent at the open with oil stocks Total and Elf leading the pack after both said they were considering a share buy-back.
In currencies, the dollar suffered as Japan's March overall trade surplus fell sharply but posted an 11.2 percent rise with the United States, heightening trade tension between the two countries.
U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers warned overnight of trade friction unless Japan became less reliant on exports and promoted growth from within.
Senior Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara said overnight that there was growing political pressure for Japan to raise its official discount rate, which also underpinned the yen.

"As time progresses and the economy looks like coming out of recession, this pressure to raise rates will increase and will go a long way to take the pressure off dollar/yen," said Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull's Davies.
Investors are focused on U.S. February trade data for due at 1230 GMT, particularly the U.S.-Japan gap, which many expected to show continued widening.

On the interest rate front, Federal Reserve vice chair Alice Rivlin was quoted as saying on Wednesday she had voted for the recent rise in U.S. rates, although was unsure whether further rate hikes were needed to cool the economy.

But Rivlin added the U.S. economy was growing "faster than is sustainable", leading market analysts to believe Rivlin and the rest of the Fed governors would vote to raise rates again at its May 20 meeting.
CURRENCIES AT 0915 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7279 marks and 125.71 yen after ending at 1.7285 and 125.80 in late trading in Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0915 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 2.7 points at 4,297.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 10.21 points at 2,631.18.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 29.64 points at 3,383.09.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in London at $341.20 versus $339.65 at the close in London on Wednesday. Silver was four cents high er at $4.84.
